title: Jibril — the Trustworthy Spirit
subtitle: The angel who carried every word of the final revelation
sources: Qur'an 2:97 — 'it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart'
Qur'an 26:193-194 — 'The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down Upon your heart'
Qur'an 96:1 — the first word of revelation, in the cave of Hira
Sahih al-Bukhari 3 — the first revelation in Hira (Aisha)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3232 and Sahih Muslim 174 — Ibn Mas'ud: the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril with six hundred wings
Sahih Muslim 8 — the hadith of Jibril in human form (Umar)

chapters.heading: Iqra
chapters.body: He came to a man in a cave and said: Iqra — Read (Bukhari 3; the first verses are 96:1-5). The Qur'an calls him the Trustworthy Spirit and says of the revelation: 'The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down Upon your heart, [O Muhammad] - that you may be of the warners' (26:193-194), and it names him Gabriel as the one who 'has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart, [O Muhammad], by permission of Allah' (2:97). Ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his own form, with six hundred wings (Bukhari 3232; Muslim 174). On another day Jibril came as a man — in pure white clothes, his hair extraordinarily black, with no sign of travel on him — sat before the Prophet ﷺ and asked about Islam, iman, ihsan and the Hour. When he had gone the Prophet ﷺ told Umar: that was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion (Muslim 8). Every verse of the Qur'an recited tonight anywhere on earth reached humanity through the revelation he brought.

familyQuestion: Jibril came as a man and asked questions so that the Companions would learn their religion. What question could you ask tonight that would teach your whole family something?

title: Mika'il — Named Beside Jibril
subtitle: What the Qur'an and the sound hadith say of him — and where they stop
sources: Qur'an 2:98 — named with Jibril as an angel of Allah
Sahih Muslim 770 — the Prophet's ﷺ night-prayer opening: 'Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil' (Aisha)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4054 and Sahih Muslim 2306 — Uhud: two men in white at the Prophet's ﷺ side (Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas)

chapters.heading: Named in the Qur'an
chapters.body: Mika'il is named once in the Qur'an, together with Jibril: 'Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers' (2:98). Aisha reported that when the Prophet ﷺ got up at night he began his prayer by calling on Allah as Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen (Muslim 770). And Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reported that on the day of Uhud he saw two men in white clothes, on the right and the left of the Prophet ﷺ, fighting with all their strength, whom he had never seen before or after (Bukhari 4054); in Muslim's report they were Jibril and Mika'il (Muslim 2306). Beyond this the Qur'an and the hadith checked for this card say little about him. Later tradition describes his charge as rain and provision; no verse or hadith checked here says so, and this card does not present it as established.

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ began his night prayer by naming the Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil. When did you last begin a prayer by thinking about who you are standing before?

title: Israfil — the Trumpet
subtitle: The one with the horn is listening for the command
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills'
Qur'an 39:69 — the earth will shine with the light of its Lord
Sahih al-Bukhari 4814 — 'forty' between the two blowings (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 770 — Israfil named in the Prophet's ﷺ night-prayer opening (Aisha)
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2431 — 'the one with the horn' awaiting the command (hasan per al-Tirmidhi; sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam — graders differ)

chapters.heading: The Longest Silence in Creation
chapters.body: The Qur'an describes the Horn: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on' (39:68). The Prophet ﷺ said there will be forty between the two blowings, and when Abu Hurayrah was asked whether he meant forty days, forty years or forty months, he would only say that he refused to say (Bukhari 4814). The Prophet ﷺ also said: how can I be at ease while the one with the horn has put the horn to his lips, listening for the command to blow? And when it weighed on the Companions he taught them to say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs (Tirmidhi 2431: al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan, al-Albani sahih, and Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam da'if, so graders differ). That hadith says 'the one with the horn' and does not name him. The tradition names the angel Israfil — Ibn Kathir says so in his tafsir — and Israfil is named, as an angel, in the Prophet's night-prayer opening (Muslim 770). Think about what the wait means: the blast has not yet sounded, and every day that passes is a day in which turning back is still open to you (a reflection, not a report). The Qur'an adds that on that Day the earth will shine with the light of its Lord and the record will be placed (39:69).

familyQuestion: The blast has not yet sounded. If you knew it was close, what would you put right tonight?

title: Malak al-Mawt — the Angel of Death
subtitle: 'He has been entrusted with you' — and then you are returned to your Lord
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — 'Say, The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you'
Qur'an 16:32 — the angels take the righteous saying 'Peace be upon you'
Qur'an 8:50 — the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved
Qur'an 6:61 — 'Our messengers take him'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer given glad tidings at death and longing to meet Allah

chapters.heading: The Gentle Taking
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers the question no one can escape: 'Say, The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you. Then to your Lord you will be returned' (32:11). Entrusted with you: the taking of your soul is a duty given to the angel by Allah, and other verses speak of Allah's messengers — the angels — who take a soul when death comes (6:61). The Qur'an says the angels take the righteous saying: 'Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do' (16:32). And a hadith says that when death comes the believer is given news of Allah's pleasure and honour, and so longs to meet Him, while the disbeliever is given news of punishment and dreads the meeting (Bukhari 6507). The taking of those who disbelieved is described very differently: the angels strike their faces and their backs (8:50). Same angel, two very different meetings — in the sources the difference is not the angel but the state of the soul he meets (a reflection on 16:32 and 8:50).

familyQuestion: The Qur'an says you will be returned to your Lord. What would you want your record to say on the day you are returned?

title: The Scribes on Your Shoulders
subtitle: Noble recorders, knowing whatever you do — writing right now
sources: Qur'an 82:10-12 — 'Noble and recording; They know whatever you do'
Qur'an 50:17-18 — 'when the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left'
Qur'an 17:14 — 'Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant'
Sahih Muslim 129 — the angels and the servant who intends a deed (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: The Two Receivers
chapters.body: The Qur'an says that over every person are appointed keepers: 'Noble and recording; They know whatever you do' (82:11-12). It describes two of them: 'When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left. Man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared [to record]' (50:17-18). The Qur'an does not say which side writes what; that the right-hand one writes the good and the left-hand one the evil is a common saying that this card does not claim. The hadith adds mercy to the record: Allah said that when His servant intends a good deed and does not do it, one good deed is written for him, and when he intends an evil deed and does not do it, He forgives that; the angels are told to watch the one who intends evil, and if he leaves it for Allah's sake a good deed is written for him (Muslim 129). On the Day the book is presented: 'Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant' (17:14). Nothing you have done is missing from the record — and an evil you only intended and then left for Allah's sake is written as a good deed, not held against you.

familyQuestion: Allah writes a good deed even for the good you only intended. What good are you hesitating to carry out right now?

title: Munkar & Nakir — the Two Questioners
subtitle: The questions of the grave — told to prepare, never to terrorize
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1071 — the two angels Al-Munkar and An-Nakir (hasan per al-Albani)
Sunan Abi Dawud 4753 — the longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is the man sent among you? (sahih per al-Albani)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1369 — al-Bara': 14:27 was revealed concerning the questioning in the grave
Qur'an 14:27 — 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter'

chapters.heading: Man Rabbuka?
chapters.body: Two angels come to the one who has been buried, the hadith teaches. Abu Hurayrah reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that their names are Al-Munkar and An-Nakir, and that they ask what he used to say about this man, the Prophet ﷺ (Tirmidhi 1071, hasan per al-Albani). The longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib gives three questions: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? What do you say about the man who was sent among you? The believer answers: my Lord is Allah; my religion is Islam; he is the Messenger of Allah. A caller from heaven says: My servant has spoken the truth; a door to Paradise is opened for him, and his grave is made wide for him as far as the eye can see (Abu Dawud 4753, sahih per al-Albani). Al-Bara' reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that the verse 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter' (14:27) was revealed concerning this (Bukhari 1369). The design rule this library keeps: the grave is told in order to prepare, never to terrorize — the answers are learned in the living room, not in the grave.

familyQuestion: The three questions are about knowing, not performing. Could you answer all three tonight, out loud, in one sentence each?

title: The Angels You Never See
subtitle: The dhikr circles' witnesses, the ameen of heaven, and the companions assigned to every person
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6408 — the angels who seek circles of dhikr and surround them with their wings (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2732 — the angel who answers your dua for your absent brother
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1282 — angels who convey the greetings of the ummah to the Prophet ﷺ (sahih per al-Albani)
Sahih Muslim 2814 — every person has an assigned companion from the jinn, and in one wording one from the angels too (Ibn Mas'ud)

chapters.heading: The Sky Fills Up
chapters.body: When people sit remembering Allah, the hadith says that angels who roam the roads looking for such gatherings call to one another, surround the people with their wings up to the lowest heaven, and Allah asks the angels about them, and says: I make you witnesses that I have forgiven them (Bukhari 6408). The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah has angels who travel the earth and convey to him the greetings of his ummah (Nasa'i 1282, sahih per al-Albani). When you make dua for your brother in his absence, the angel appointed over it says: Amen, and the same be for you too (Muslim 2732). And the Prophet ﷺ said that every one of us has been assigned a companion from the jinn — in one wording, a companion from the angels as well — and when the Companions asked if that applied to him, he said yes, but Allah helped him against it, so it commands him only to good (Muslim 2814). You are never as alone in a room as it feels.

familyQuestion: A gathering of dhikr fills the sky with witnesses. When did you last sit with people remembering Allah — and could you this week?

title: The Bearers of the Throne & the Six Hundred Wings
subtitle: Eight will bear the Throne on the Day when the whole earth is in His grip
sources: Qur'an 69:17 — 'And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them'
Qur'an 39:75 and 40:7 — the angels around the Throne, and those who bear it, glorify their Lord
Qur'an 35:1 — angels 'having wings, two or three or four'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3232 — Jibril's six hundred wings (Ibn Mas'ud)

chapters.heading: The Size of the Unseen
chapters.body: The Qur'an says that Allah made the angels messengers 'having wings, two or three or four', and adds that He increases in creation what He wills (35:1). Ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril with six hundred wings (Bukhari 3232); further scenery sometimes told of that sighting is not in the report and is not repeated here. Of the Day itself the Qur'an says: 'And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight [of them]' (69:17); Ibn Kathir explains this as eight angels. And the Qur'an records what those who bear the Throne, and those around it, say: they exalt their Lord with praise, believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed — 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire' (40:7). The largest beings the sources describe spend their worship praising Allah and praying for the believers — and you are among those they pray for.

familyQuestion: The bearers of the Throne ask forgiveness for the believers (40:7). When did you last ask forgiveness for the believers, by name?

title: Created from Smokeless Fire
subtitle: Created before mankind, from fire — and, like us, made to worship
sources: Qur'an 15:27 — 'the jinn We created before from scorching fire'
Qur'an 55:15 — 'He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire'
Qur'an 72:11 — the jinn: righteous and otherwise
Qur'an 51:56 — 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me'

chapters.heading: An Older People
chapters.body: The Qur'an says the jinn were created before mankind: 'And the jinn We created before from scorching fire' (15:27) — and 'He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire' (55:15). They are not ghosts and not metaphors. The Qur'an treats them as a real created people who are addressed and held to account, with righteous and not-so-righteous among them (72:11), like ours: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). Knowing they exist changes the weather of the night: you are not the only audience in the room, and the One who made both nations sees both at once. The app's rule is the Qur'an's rule: tell what is revealed, and let the rest stay veiled — what the sources do not tell us, this app does not guess at.

familyQuestion: Allah made two nations to worship Him — ours and theirs. What does that tell you about how big the creation really is?

title: Iblis Refuses
subtitle: The Qur'an says he was of the jinn — and his argument is still in use
sources: Qur'an 2:34 — 'when We said to the angels, Prostrate before Adam; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused'
Qur'an 18:50 — 'He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord'
Qur'an 7:12 — 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay'
Qur'an 15:34-35 — expelled, with the curse until the Day of Recompense

chapters.heading: I Am Better Than Him
chapters.body: The Qur'an is precise: Iblis 'was of the jinn' (18:50), yet he was among those addressed when Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam (2:34), and he refused. (Scholars have discussed how a jinn came to be among the angels' company; the Qur'an's own words are the starting point and are what this card keeps to) — and his refusal had an argument: 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay' (7:12). Look at the anatomy of the fall: comparison, pride, and then the transfer of blame — 'because You have put me in error' (15:39), as if the One who commanded good had authored his disobedience. Allah's answer: 'Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled. And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense' (15:34-35). Every arrogance you have ever felt — I'm better than him, I deserve more than her — echoes that same sentence in a smaller voice (reflection). Pride and comparison are the root the Qur'an shows beneath his refusal (reflection).

familyQuestion: Iblis's fall began with comparing himself to someone. When did comparison last poison your contentment?

title: The Open Vow
subtitle: 'Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all'
sources: Qur'an 15:36-38 — 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected' — granted until 'the Day of the time well-known'
Qur'an 38:82 — 'By your might, I will surely mislead them all'
Qur'an 7:16-17 — 'then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left'
Qur'an 15:42 — 'Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators'

chapters.heading: Reprieved on Purpose
chapters.body: Iblis asked for time — not forgiveness: 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected' (15:36) — and Allah answered that he was among those reprieved until the Day of the time well-known (15:37-38): the trial of temptation runs until then. His strategy is mapped in the Qur'an: 'Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful' (7:17) (reflection: the verse names four directions; it does not mention above, and some commentators draw lessons from that — the card does not rest anything on it). And note the promise within the threat: he swore by Allah's might to mislead them all (38:82), and the Qur'an answers: 'Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators' (15:42). His reach has a border. The border is: those who do not follow.

familyQuestion: Shaytan was reprieved to test us — the test is the point. What is the hardest thing about being tested on purpose?

title: The Whisper — Waswas
subtitle: Not a command — a suggestion, thin as breath
sources: Qur'an 114:4-6 — 'From the evil of the retreating whisperer - Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind - From among the jinn and mankind'
Qur'an 7:200 — 'And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah'
Sahih Muslim 134 — when Shaytan asks 'who created Allah?', seek refuge in Allah and stop (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: A Suggestion, Not a Voice
chapters.body: The Qur'an never has Shaytan forcing anyone. He whispers — waswas — 'Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind - From among the jinn and mankind' (114:5-6). Two sources of whisper: the jinn, and other people. The Qur'an gives the answer before the whisper arrives: 'And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing' (7:200). A common image (not a quotation from the sources) compares it to a passing bird: it lands on your branch and does not build a nest unless you let it stay. The Qur'an's instruction is to seek refuge in Allah (7:200), and the Prophet ﷺ taught that Shaytan comes to a person asking who created this and that until he asks who created your Lord; when it reaches that, one should seek refuge in Allah and stop (Muslim 134, from Abu Hurayrah). You cannot stop birds from flying over your head. You can stop them from nesting in your hair.

familyQuestion: The whisper only lands where it is welcomed. What branch of your life has a bird sitting on it right now?

title: Your Constant Companion
subtitle: Every person has a companion assigned from the jinn
sources: Sahih Muslim 2814 (Ibn Mas'ud) — 'there is none among you but a companion from the jinn has been assigned to him' — and in Sufyan's wording, a companion from the angels as well

chapters.heading: The Jinn Beside You
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught what no eye can verify: each of you has had a companion from the jinn assigned to him (a qarin); in one wording of the same hadith there is also an assigned companion from the angels. The Companions asked: even you, O Messenger of Allah? — and he said: even me, except that Allah helped me against him, and he submitted (fa-aslama), so he commands me only to good (Muslim 2814, from Ibn Mas'ud). Scholars read the word fa-aslama in two ways — he became Muslim, or I am safe from his harm — and both readings agree that the Prophet ﷺ was protected from his companion's evil; this card does not choose between them. The hadith hands you two facts: the companion is with every person, and the Prophet's own example shows the pressure can be overcome with Allah's help. The hadith does not describe what the companion says or how it works, and this card does not add to it.

familyQuestion: Allah helped the Prophet ﷺ against his companion. What help from Allah are you asking for against your own worst inner voice?

title: Possession & the Evil Eye
subtitle: What the sources confirm — and what they do not
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3268 — the Prophet ﷺ was bewitched, shown the cause, and cured by Allah (Aisha)
Sahih Muslim 2188 — the evil eye is real (Ibn Abbas)
Sahih Muslim 2200 — ruqyah is permitted if it contains no shirk (Awf ibn Malik)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5016 — the Prophet ﷺ recited the Mu'awwidhat over himself when ill (Aisha)
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2059 — ruqyah for the evil eye (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam)

chapters.heading: Afflicted, and Still the Messenger
chapters.body: Aisha reported that magic was worked on the Prophet ﷺ so that he began to fancy he was doing something he was not doing; he prayed at length, and then told her that Allah had shown him the cure. Two men had come to him in a dream and told him what the ailment was, who did it (Labid ibn al-A'sam) and where it was, and Allah cured him (Bukhari 3268). The report does not call this a possession and says nothing of knots or of particular verses; later accounts that add them are not in the hadith checked here, and this card does not repeat them. The evil eye is also real: Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that its influence is a fact (Muslim 2188), and he allowed ruqyah, the recitation of Qur'an and supplications, for it (Tirmidhi 2059, sahih per al-Albani and per Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam). Awf ibn Malik asked about the incantations they used before Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ said there is no harm in ruqyah as long as it contains no shirk (Muslim 2200). When he was ill the Prophet ﷺ recited the Mu'awwidhat — al-Falaq and an-Nas — and blew over himself (Bukhari 5016, from Aisha). The sources checked for this card do not set out rules for diagnosing possession; if you are afflicted, the safe course is the revealed words, the doctor, and a trusted scholar.

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ was afflicted and Allah cured him. What difficulty are you carrying that you have not yet brought to Allah and to a qualified helper?

title: Sulayman's Jinn
subtitle: A kingdom of builders — and a lesson about borrowed power
sources: Qur'an 34:12-14 — the jinn who worked for Sulayman, and the staff
Qur'an 21:82 — 'And of the devils were those who dived for him and did work other than that'
Qur'an 38:37-38 — 'every builder and diver And others bound together in shackles'

chapters.heading: Builders on a Leash
chapters.body: Allah subjected some of the jinn to Sulayman as part of the kingdom he was granted (34:12): they built him lofty halls, statues, basins like reservoirs, and great fixed cauldrons (34:13); some were divers (38:37), some did other work (21:82); and the rebellious among them were kept 'bound together in shackles' (38:38). The Qur'an adds the detail that keeps the whole picture honest: 'And when We decreed for Solomon death, nothing indicated to the jinn his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff. But when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment' (34:14). The jinn kept working until the staff gave way and he fell; only then did it become clear to them that they did not have knowledge of the unseen. A reflection: every power that serves you — wealth, health, people — is held up by Allah's decree.

familyQuestion: The jinn kept working without knowing the king had died. What are you serving without checking whether it still stands by Allah's permission?

title: The Ifrit and the Throne of the Queen of Sheba
subtitle: One jinn's boast, and one man's knowledge of the Scripture
sources: Qur'an 27:22-23 — the hoopoe's report of a woman ruling Sheba, with a great throne
Qur'an 27:38-40 — the ifrit from among the jinn, and 'one who had knowledge from the Scripture'

chapters.heading: I Will Bring It Before You Stand
chapters.body: The hoopoe told Sulayman of a woman ruling the people of Sheba who 'has been given of all things, and she has a great throne' (27:22-23). The Qur'an does not name her; the name Bilqis comes from later tradition. Before the Sabaeans came to him in submission, Sulayman asked his council: 'O assembly [of jinn], which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?' (27:38). 'A powerful one from among the jinn' — an ifrit — said: 'I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [task] strong and trustworthy' (27:39). Then 'one who had knowledge from the Scripture' said: 'I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you' (27:40). The Qur'an does not name him; commentators have suggested names, and the card follows the verse. When Sulayman saw the throne placed before him he did not boast: 'This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful' (27:40). The scene shows a jinn's strength, a believer's knowledge, and the king who credits it all to his Lord.

familyQuestion: Sulayman saw the impossible and said, 'This is from the favor of my Lord to test me.' What favor in your life do you need to see as a test of gratitude?

title: Jinn Who Heard the Qur'an
subtitle: A group of them heard the Qur'an and believed
sources: Qur'an 72:1-2 — 'a group of the jinn listened and said: Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an'
Qur'an 46:29-32 — 'a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an'
Sahih al-Bukhari 773 — Ibn Abbas: the jinn who heard the Fajr recitation at Nakhla
Sahih Muslim 450 — the night the Prophet ﷺ recited to the jinn (Ibn Mas'ud)

chapters.heading: The Jinn Who Listened
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells of a few of the jinn who listened (Surah al-Ahqaf, 46:29), and they went back to their people as warners: 'O our people, indeed we have heard a [recited] Book revealed after Moses confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path ... O our people, respond to the Messenger of Allah and believe in him' (46:30-31). Ibn Abbas reports (Bukhari 773) that the Prophet ﷺ set out with some companions toward the market of Ukaz; the jinn had been barred from the news of heaven, so they sent scouts in different directions, and one group found him at Nakhla leading the Fajr prayer. They listened to the Qur'an, returned to their people and said they had heard a wonderful recital and believed in it (Bukhari 773), and Surah al-Jinn was revealed: 'Say, [O Muhammad], It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an. It guides to the right course, and we have believed in it' (72:1-2). Some of the unseen heard the Qur'an, and some of them believed. (Muslim 450 reports a further night on which the Prophet ﷺ went out and recited to the jinn.)

familyQuestion: Jinn converted by overhearing Fajr recitation. What does that say about what your own recitation could be doing unseen?

title: Jinn Who Believe, and Shaytan Who Flees
subtitle: Righteous and otherwise — and Shaytan flees the adhan
sources: Qur'an 72:11 — 'among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so'
Sahih Muslim 450 — bones and dung are not for istinja: they are the provision of the jinn (Ibn Mas'ud)
Sahih al-Bukhari 608 — Shaytan flees the adhan (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3275 — Ayat al-Kursi before sleep: a guardian from Allah (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: Shared Earth
chapters.body: The jinn speak of themselves in the Qur'an: 'among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so; we were [of] divided ways' (72:11). Some believe and some do not. The hadith also tells that Shaytan flees when the adhan is called, passing wind so that he does not hear it (Bukhari 608). On the night the jinn were recited to, the Prophet ﷺ was asked about their provision and said that every bone on which Allah's name is recited will be in their hands covered with flesh; and he told the Companions not to use bones or dung for istinja, for they are the food of your brothers among the jinn (Muslim 450, from Ibn Mas'ud). Abu Hurayrah's report of the captured thief adds that whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi when he goes to bed has a guardian from Allah over him until morning, and Shaytan cannot approach (Bukhari 3275). The sources say nothing more about the jinn in mosques or graveyards, and this card does not either. The rule of the library: knowledge is protection, not a playground.

familyQuestion: Shaytan runs from the adhan. When you hear it and keep sitting, which of you is more disciplined?

title: Why You Cannot See Them
subtitle: Veiled by design — and by mercy
sources: Qur'an 7:27 — 'he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them'
Qur'an 50:22 — 'We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp'
Sahih Muslim 8 — ihsan: 'to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you'

chapters.heading: One-Way Glass
chapters.body: The veil runs one direction: 'Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them' (7:27). They see you; you do not see them — (7:27 is a warning to the children of Adam). One can reflect that the veil is also a mercy — but that is a reflection and not a statement of the verse. The Qur'an says that on the Day of Resurrection the covering is removed — 'You were certainly in unmindfulness of this, and We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp' (50:22). Until then, the evidence is the Qur'an and the sound sunnah, and the demand is ihsan as the Prophet ﷺ defined it to Jibril: to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you (Muslim 8).

familyQuestion: You are watched but not stalked — seen but given privacy. How would you live differently if the veil lifted for one day?

title: Protection from the Jinn
subtitle: A few short habits taught by the Prophet ﷺ
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3275 — Ayat al-Kursi before sleep: a guardian from Allah remains over you (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5017 — al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas, blown into the hands and wiped over the body at bedtime (Aisha)
Sunan Abi Dawud 5082 — the three quls three times, morning and evening, will suffice you (hasan per al-Albani; isnad hasan per Zubair Ali Za'i)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3269 — the three knots of Shaytan and how they are undone (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2018 — naming Allah on entering the house (Jabir)
Qur'an 2:255 — Ayat al-Kursi

chapters.heading: The Fortress
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught his companions habits, not investigations. Ayat al-Kursi before sleep: whoever recites it has a guardian from Allah over him, and Shaytan will not approach till dawn (Bukhari 3275). Aisha reported that every night when he went to bed he cupped his hands, blew into them after reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas, and wiped over what he could reach of his body, three times (Bukhari 5017). Abdullah ibn Khubayb reported that the Prophet ﷺ told him to recite al-Ikhlas and the two Mu'awwidhat three times in the morning and the evening, and that they suffice him (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani). When a man enters his house and mentions Allah's name, Shaytan says: no place for you to spend the night, no supper (Muslim 2018, from Jabir). And the Prophet ﷺ said that during your sleep Shaytan ties three knots at the back of your head, saying: the night is long, so keep on sleeping; if you wake and mention Allah one knot is undone, if you make wudu the second, and if you pray the last, and you get up in the morning lively (Bukhari 3269). The fortress is made of habit, not fear.

familyQuestion: The protection is short habits, not hours of fear. Which of them are you missing most nights?

title: Play 1: Comparison
subtitle: He turns blessings into evidence against you
sources: Qur'an 7:12 — Iblis's comparison: 'I am better than him'
Qur'an 7:23 — Adam and Hawwa: 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves'
Qur'an 20:122 — 'then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him'
Sahih Muslim 2963 — look at those below you in wealth, so you do not belittle Allah's favours (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: The Measuring Stick
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the soul 'a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy' (12:53). A reflection on the pattern: one common instrument is the measuring stick — look at their house, their waist, their followers, their ease. The Qur'an shows the antidote built into Adam's story — after the fall, he said with his wife: 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers' (7:23), and Allah 'turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him]' (20:122). Comparison is the argument the Qur'an records from Iblis ('I am better than him' — 7:12). The Prophet ﷺ gave a counter-move for wealth: look at the one who is below you, not at the one above you, for that is better-suited so that you do not belittle the favours of Allah (Muslim 2963, from Abu Hurayrah). You cannot stop the measuring stick from being shown to you. You can refuse to hold it.

familyQuestion: Comparison was the first word of the first devil. What are you measuring yourself against this week — and is it holding you or hurting you?

title: Play 2: Despair After Sin
subtitle: His only win is convincing you the door is locked
sources: Qur'an 39:53-54 — 'do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins' — and 'return [in repentance] to your Lord'
Qur'an 12:87 — 'despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people'

chapters.heading: The Locked-Door Lie
chapters.body: No sin locks the door. The Qur'an addresses the sinner directly, in the second person, with the widest promise in scripture: 'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful' (39:53) — all sins, to a people addressed as still His servants even in their transgression. Shaytan's whisper after a fall can sound like: you knew better; you've gone too far; the prayer is pointless now (a reflection on the pattern, not a report). A reflection on the pattern: after a sin, the thing that most blocks the return is despair, and the Qur'an closes it off directly. The verse that follows says: 'And return [in repentance] to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you' (39:54). The evidence: Ya'qub, who lost two sons and a whole lifetime, told his children: 'go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people' (12:87) — he named despair itself the disbelief. The door has no lock on the inside.

familyQuestion: The widest promise in scripture is addressed to people in the middle of their sin. What door have you been treating as locked?

title: Play 3: The Delay Tactic
subtitle: He does not tell you 'no' — he tells you 'later'
sources: Qur'an 59:18-19 — 'And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves'
Qur'an 63:10-11 — 'if only You would delay me for a brief term' — but 'never will Allah delay a soul when its time has come'
Sahih Muslim 118 — 'Be prompt in doing good deeds before you are overtaken by turbulence like a part of the dark night' (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: Tomorrow's Trap
chapters.body: A reflection on the pattern (not a report): delay can sound reasonable — 'pray after this message,' 'repent when Ramadan comes.' The Qur'an names the danger of forgetting Allah in one breath: 'And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient' (59:19). The Qur'an records the plea of the one who waited: 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous' — and the answer: 'But never will Allah delay a soul when its time has come' (63:10-11). And the Prophet ﷺ urged haste: be prompt in doing good deeds before you are overtaken by turbulence like a part of the dark night (Muslim 118, from Abu Hurayrah). The counter-scheduling is to do the good deed immediately, small and now, before the whispers can open their calendar.

familyQuestion: He never says no — he says later. What is the one small good thing you could do in the next five minutes, ending one 'later' tonight?

title: Play 4: The Loop
subtitle: Shame feeds the sin that feeds the shame — break it with a sentence
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — the promise repeated over every returning sinner
Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity'
Qur'an 3:135 — 'remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins'

chapters.heading: The Engine of Return
chapters.body: Secret sins run on an engine: sin, then shame, then the shame says you are the kind of person who sins, and that identity licenses the next sin — the loop closes itself. The devil does not need to tempt you each round; your shame does his work. The break is not willpower; it is a sentence said in the moment of shame — the Qur'an describes those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins (3:135). And the door of tawbah is not a yearly gate: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah accepts the servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat (Tirmidhi 3537, hasan per Darussalam). The loop ends where it started: not with a perfect week, but with one turning — and the turning is available at 2am, mid-fall, mid-shame, every single time.

familyQuestion: The shame is not the punishment — it's the trap. What sentence could you say out loud tonight to break one loop?

title: Play 5: Anger & Argument
subtitle: Seek refuge, sit down, answer with better
sources: Qur'an 41:34 — 'Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6114 — 'the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger' (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2610 and Bukhari 3282 — 'I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed' (Sulayman ibn Surad)
Sunan Abi Dawud 4782 — if angry while standing, sit; otherwise lie down (sahih per al-Albani; Abu Dharr)

chapters.heading: The Oil
chapters.body: The Qur'an says Iblis said he was created from fire (7:12); the sources checked here do not state that anger is made of fire, and this card does not claim it. Sulayman ibn Surad reported that two men abused each other before the Prophet ﷺ, and one's face reddened and his neck veins swelled; the Prophet ﷺ said: I know a word that, if he said it, would remove what he feels: 'I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed' (Muslim 2610; Bukhari 3282). A reflection on the pattern: in an argument the danger is escalation — make him say the unforgivable thing, make her win at any cost, make the marriage, the friendship, the business partnership pay the price of one hot evening. The Prophet ﷺ taught the physical counter: when one of you becomes angry while standing, he should sit; if the anger leaves him, well and good, otherwise he should lie down (Abu Dawud 4782, from Abu Dharr; sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam). And the Qur'an gives the moral counter: 'Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend' (41:34). Seek refuge, sit, and answer with better.

familyQuestion: Seeking refuge, sitting down, answering better — which of these could you use in the argument you are in right now?

title: Play 6: Fame and the Hidden Sin
subtitle: He applauds your goodness when someone is watching
sources: Qur'an 107:4-6 — 'So woe to those who pray [But] who are heedless of their prayer - Those who make show [of their deeds]'
Sahih Muslim 1905 — the first three judged: the martyr, the reciter and the wealthy man who did it to be seen
Sahih al-Bukhari 660 — the seven shaded by Allah's shade; the hidden charity

chapters.heading: The Applause Trap
chapters.body: The hadith that should keep every visible believer awake: the first people judged on the Day are three — a martyr, a scholar and reciter of the Qur'an, and a wealthy man who spent. Each tells Allah what he did for Him, and Allah answers that he did it so that it would be said: a brave man, a scholar, a generous man — and it was said. Each is dragged on his face into the Fire (Muslim 1905, from Abu Hurayrah). The Qur'an speaks of those 'who make show [of their deeds]' (107:6). A reflection on the pattern: the danger the hadith warns of is worship turned toward an audience — the sadaqah announced, the knowledge performed. The antidote is a hidden habit the size of a seed: the Prophet ﷺ said seven are shaded by Allah's shade on the Day when there is no shade but His — among them a man who gives charity so hidden that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given (Bukhari 660). Let some of your good be known only to the One who counts it.

familyQuestion: Three heroes of the world were told 'your wage was paid in applause.' What good thing could you do this week that no one but Allah will ever know about?

title: The Last Breath
subtitle: The shudder, the brightness, and the family left at the door
sources: Qur'an 50:19 — 'the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid'
Sahih Muslim 916 — prompt the dying to say la ilaha illa Allah (Abu Sa'id al-Khudri)
Sahih Muslim 920 — the Prophet ﷺ closed Abu Salamah's eyes (Umm Salamah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5814 — the Prophet's ﷺ body was covered when he died (Aisha)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1315 — hurry with the funeral (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 927 — 'the deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over him' (Umar; scholars discuss its precise meaning)
Sahih Muslim 1631 — the three deeds that continue (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: Sakarat
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the moment with one word: sakarat — the stupor of death: 'the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid' (50:19). The Prophet ﷺ taught the etiquette of the dying room: prompt the one leaving to say la ilaha illa Allah (Muslim 916, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri). When Abu Salamah died the Prophet ﷺ closed his eyes (Muslim 920, from Umm Salamah); the Prophet's own body was covered with a garment when he died (Bukhari 5814, from Aisha); and he said to hurry with the funeral (Bukhari 1315, from Abu Hurayrah). Umar reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that the deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over him (Muslim 927); scholars differ on what this means, so this card gives the hadith and leaves its explanation to a scholar. And to the family left at the door, the Prophet ﷺ said: when a man dies his deeds come to an end except three — recurring charity, knowledge by which people benefit, or a pious son who prays for him (Muslim 1631, from Abu Hurayrah). The last breath ends the deeds you can still do; these three continue.

familyQuestion: Three things reach the dead: charity, knowledge, a praying child. Which of the three are you building for your parents right now?

title: Glad Tidings at Death
subtitle: What the Qur'an and sound hadith say of the believer's soul at death
sources: Qur'an 16:32 — 'The ones whom the angels take in death, [being] good and pure; [the angels] will say, Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do'
Qur'an 32:11 — 'The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you'
Qur'an 3:169-170 — those killed in the cause of Allah are alive with their Lord
Sahih Muslim 1887 — the souls of the martyrs in green birds (Ibn Mas'ud)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer's glad tidings at death (Ubadah ibn as-Samit)
Qur'an 100:9 — the contents of the graves scattered

chapters.heading: Carried Upward
chapters.body: The Qur'an says the angels take the righteous saying: 'Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do' (16:32), and Ubadah ibn as-Samit reported that when a believer's death approaches he receives the good news of Allah's pleasure and blessings, and nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead (Bukhari 6507). The souls of the martyrs are described specifically: Masruq asked Ibn Mas'ud about 3:169, and he said they had asked the Prophet ﷺ, who said that the souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds with nests in lamps hung from the Throne, which eat of Paradise wherever they wish (Muslim 1887); and the Qur'an speaks of those killed in Allah's cause as alive with their Lord, receiving provision and rejoicing (3:169-170). The Qur'an also speaks of the day 'the contents of the graves are scattered' (100:9). Every soul is raised; the Qur'an leaves the believer with glad tidings and the denier with warning.

familyQuestion: Glad tidings at death are for the believer. What would you want to be said to you at that moment?

title: The Grave and What Is Shown There
subtitle: Shown his place morning and evening; widened for the believer
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1379 and Sahih Muslim 2866 — the deceased is shown his place morning and evening (Ibn Umar)
Sunan Abi Dawud 4753 — the longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: the believer's grave widened as far as the eye can see (sahih per al-Albani)
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1071 — 'Sleep as a newlywed' (hasan per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: Widened as Far as the Eye Can See
chapters.body: Ibn Umar reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that when one of you dies he is shown his place morning and evening: if he is from the people of Paradise, his place there; if from the people of the Fire, his place there; and it is said to him, this is your place until Allah raises you (Bukhari 1379; Muslim 2866). For the believer, the longer report of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib says that after he answers the angels a caller from heaven says that His servant has spoken the truth, a bed from Paradise is spread for him, a door to Paradise is opened, some of its air and perfume reach him, and his grave is made wide as far as the eye can see (Abu Dawud 4753, sahih per al-Albani). In Abu Hurayrah's report the believer's grave is expanded to seventy cubits by seventy and lit for him, and he is told to sleep like a bridegroom whom only the dearest of his family wakes, until Allah raises him (Tirmidhi 1071, hasan per al-Albani). The sources describe how the believer is shown and honoured; they do not describe the nature of the grave's world beyond these words, and this card does not add to them. The reflection that follows is ours: this is why the believer prepares, not why he is afraid.

familyQuestion: The grave is shown to be a place of honour for the one who answers well. What are you preparing to answer with?

title: Barzakh — The Barrier
subtitle: A barrier between two worlds
sources: Qur'an 23:99-100 — 'behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected'
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the blast, and the cry 'Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?'
Sahih al-Bukhari 1379 — shown his place morning and evening (Ibn Umar)
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2308 — 'the grave is the first stage among the stages of the Hereafter' (hasan per al-Albani; isnad hasan per Zubair Ali Za'i)

chapters.heading: The Waiting Place
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the interval: barzakh — a barrier. Of the one who asks to be sent back it says: 'and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100). The Prophet ﷺ said that the grave is the first of the stages of the Hereafter: if one is saved from it, what comes after is easier, and if not, what comes after is harder (Tirmidhi 2308, from Uthman; hasan per al-Albani). The deceased is shown his place morning and evening (Bukhari 1379). When the Horn is blown the Qur'an records the cry 'O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?' (36:52). How the barzakh is experienced is among the matters of the unseen on which the sources say little, and this card says no more than they do.

familyQuestion: The barzakh is a barrier between two worlds. If tonight were the last night of this one, what would you want to have put right?

title: The Trial of the Grave — and Its Shields
subtitle: Established in the hadith — and the shields the Prophet ﷺ named
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1374 — the grave's questioning, the believer's seat in Paradise and the hammers
Sahih Muslim 1913 — the one who guards the frontier is kept safe from the tester of the grave
Qur'an 40:45-46 — 'they are exposed to it morning and evening' for Pharaoh's people

chapters.heading: The Trial and the Shields
chapters.body: The trial of the grave is reported — the hadith of the two angels who sit the deceased up after the companions leave and ask what he used to say about this man, Muhammad ﷺ; the believer testifies that he is Allah's slave and messenger and is told to look at his place in the Fire, which Allah has replaced with a place in Paradise, while the hypocrite or disbeliever says 'I do not know; I used to say what the people said' and is struck with iron hammers (Bukhari 1374). But the tradition is equally firm that there is protection: the Prophet ﷺ said that one who guards the frontier for a day and night, and dies, has his deeds continue to be credited to him, his provision continues, and he is kept safe from the tester, which the translation renders as the torment of the grave (Muslim 1913, from Salman). The Qur'an describes the people of Pharaoh as exposed to the Fire 'morning and evening' before the Day the Hour appears (40:46). The card stops where the sources stop: the trial is reported, shields are named, and the believer's duty is to prepare, not to speculate.

familyQuestion: The shields are named and take five minutes. What is your morning adhkar actually like — armor, or afterthought?

title: The First Blast
subtitle: The end of the old world's tenancy
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills'
Qur'an 27:87 — 'and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills'
Sahih al-Bukhari 4814 — 'forty' between the two blasts; Abu Hurayrah declined to say days, months or years

chapters.heading: The Silence Between the Blasts
chapters.body: The Qur'an describes the scene: the whole earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection and 'the heavens will be folded in His right hand' (39:67). Then: 'whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills' (39:68). The Prophet ﷺ said there will be forty between the two blowings; Abu Hurayrah was asked whether he meant forty days, forty years or forty months, and he declined to say (Bukhari 4814). The old world's tenancy ends in one sound. The Qur'an promised it would; the universe keeps the appointment.

familyQuestion: One sound ends everything. If the appointment is certain, what deserves your worry — the sound, or what you send ahead of it?

title: The Second Blast
subtitle: Standing barefoot on a changed earth, facing the Lord of the worlds
sources: Qur'an 36:51-52 — 'And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten'
Qur'an 18:47 — the mountains removed, the earth prominent
Qur'an 14:48 — 'the day the earth will be replaced by another earth'
Qur'an 70:4 and 22:2
Sahih Muslim 2790 — the earth like a white loaf of bread
Sahih al-Bukhari 6524 — gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised
Sahih al-Bukhari 6522 — the groups at the gathering
Sahih al-Bukhari 6532 — the sweat on the Day of Resurrection

chapters.heading: At Once They Rise
chapters.body: The second blast is the waking: 'And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place? [The reply will be], This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth' (36:51-52). The earth itself is replaced (14:48) and the mountains removed (18:47); the Prophet ﷺ described the people gathered on a pale plain like a white loaf of bread, with no landmark for anyone (Muslim 2790, from Sahl ibn Sa'd), and said, 'You will meet Allah barefooted, naked, walking on feet, and uncircumcised' (Bukhari 6524, from Ibn Abbas). The Qur'an also speaks of a Day 'the extent of which is fifty thousand years' (70:4). And the Qur'an records the detail that steadies every heart: 'On the Day you see it every nursing mother will be distracted from that [child] she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people [appearing] intoxicated while they are not intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah is severe' (22:2). No one will have time for anyone but themselves — and yet: Abu Hurayrah reports that the gathering has groups: some hoping and fearing, some riding two, three or ten to a camel, and the rest driven toward the Fire (Bukhari 6522); and that on that Day people will sweat until it reaches their mouths and ears (Bukhari 6532). The rising is certain; the Prophet ﷺ taught of seven who will be in Allah's shade on that Day (Bukhari 660).

familyQuestion: On that day no one will look at anyone else. Who are you relying on besides yourself — and have you thanked them?

title: The Scales
subtitle: A grain of mustard's weight of good will be seen
sources: Qur'an 7:8-9 — 'the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth'
Qur'an 101:6-8 — heavy scales, a pleasant life
Qur'an 99:7-8 — an atom's weight of good or evil will be seen
Qur'an 36:65 — the hands and feet testify
Sahih al-Bukhari 5641 — hardship expiates sins (Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: An Atom's Weight
chapters.body: The scales are the most democratic institution in existence: 'And the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful. And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who will lose themselves for what injustice they were doing toward Our verses' (7:8-9). On the Day the Qur'an says: 'We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn' (36:65). But read the mercy folded into the precision: 'whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (99:7-8). An atom's weight is the smallest measure the verse names. Of hardship, the Prophet ﷺ said that no fatigue, disease, sorrow, sadness, hurt or distress befalls a Muslim, even the prick of a thorn, but that Allah expiates some of his sins by it (Bukhari 5641, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah).

familyQuestion: An atom's weight will be seen. What tiny good have you been treating as too small to matter?

title: The Bridge
subtitle: Everyone crosses; what differs is the light and the grip
sources: Qur'an 19:71 — 'And there is none of you except he will come to it'
Qur'an 19:72 and 57:12 — the saved, and the believers' light
Sahih Muslim 183 — the bridge, the crossing, the believers' plea

chapters.heading: Thinner Than a Hair
chapters.body: The Qur'an says: 'And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed' (19:71). Many commentators, and the long hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, connect this with the passage over the bridge set up above Hell. In that hadith the bridge has hooks, tongs and thorns like the thorn of Najd; the believers pass over within the twinkling of an eye, like lightning, like wind, like a bird, like the finest horses and camels; some escape and are safe, some are lacerated and let go, and some are pushed into the Fire (Muslim 183). Abu Sa'id added, as his own statement: 'I have come to know that the bridge would be thinner even than the hair and sharper than the sword' (Muslim 183). The next verse is the one that answers: 'Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees' (19:72). The Qur'an also gives the believers a light for that Day: 'On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right' (57:12). In the same report, believers plead for brothers who fasted, prayed and performed pilgrimage with them and are allowed to bring them out; at the end Allah takes a handful who never did any good from the Fire and casts them into the river of life (Muslim 183).

familyQuestion: Everyone comes to the bridge and the believers have a light. What are you doing now that you hope will be your light?

title: Why did Allah create me?
subtitle: The question beneath every other question
sources: Qur'an 51:56 — 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me'
Qur'an 67:2 — 'He who created death and life to test you'
Sahih Muslim 2865 — people created with a natural inclination to worship Allah; the devils led them away

chapters.heading: The Straight Answer
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers without poetry, which is its mercy: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). Worship here is wider than ritual alone in the view of many scholars (a reflection this card offers, not a quotation). The test-frame comes elsewhere in revelation: '[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed' (67:2) — life is the examination hall, not the playground and not the prison. You were made on purpose, for a purpose: the Prophet ﷺ relayed what his Lord taught him, that people were created with a natural inclination to worship Allah, and the devils came to them and led them away from their religion (Muslim 2865, the sermon of Iyad ibn Himar). The 2am answer is one sentence: you were made to know and serve your Maker, and every gift in your life is a question about how you spent it.

familyQuestion: If life is a test, which question are you currently failing on purpose?

title: What happens when I die?
subtitle: The question the app was named after
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — the entrusted taking
Qur'an 23:100 — the barrier
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the waking

chapters.heading: The Road in Four Stops
chapters.body: The road has four stops, and the Qur'an gives each one: the taking — 'The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you' (32:11); the waiting — the grave and its barzakh, 'a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100); the waking — 'the horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51); and the meeting — 'that day you will be exhibited; not hidden among you is anything concealed' (69:18). Each stage is named in the Qur'an; the experience between them is largely veiled. The 2am fear of death is, at bottom, fear of the unknown — and the Qur'an and the sound hadith give the outline. The details they do not give, this card does not add.

familyQuestion: The map exists. What is the condition of the traveler tonight — prepared, or postponing?

title: Where is Allah?
subtitle: The Throne, the jugular, and what the sources do not say
sources: Qur'an 20:5 — 'The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established'
Qur'an 50:16 — 'and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein'
Qur'an 40:7 and 69:17 — the angels who carry the Throne
Sahih Muslim 537 — the slave-girl of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam: 'Where is Allah?' (Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam)
Ibn Kathir, Tafsir of Surah Qaf 50:16 — the nearness read as the angels'

chapters.heading: Two Verses, Honestly Read
chapters.body: The Qur'an says: 'The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established' (20:5) — and the Throne is carried by angels (40:7; 69:17). It also says: 'and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein' (50:16). The tradition adds that the Prophet ﷺ asked the slave-girl of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam 'where is Allah?' and she answered: in the heaven; he asked who he was and she said: you are the Messenger of Allah; and he said: free her, for she is a believing woman (Muslim 537). Scholars read these in different ways. On 50:16, Ibn Kathir explains that 'We' refers to Allah's angels, who by His leave are nearer to a person than his jugular vein, and rejects the idea that it means Allah's being mixes with creation; others read the nearness as Allah's knowledge. On 'above the Throne' (istiwa), some affirm it as it came and leave its manner to Allah, others interpret it figuratively. This card takes no side and the question is for a scholar. What every reading agrees on is that you are known and seen by Him wherever you are, as the verse says: 'know what his soul whispers to him' (50:16).

familyQuestion: Wherever you are tonight, Allah knows what your self whispers to you. What would you want to say to Him about it?

title: Are the jinn in this room with me right now?
subtitle: The sources say they exist and see us; they do not say where they are tonight
sources: Qur'an 7:27 — 'he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them'
Sahih Muslim 2814 — an assigned companion from the jinn (Ibn Mas'ud)
Sahih Bukhari 142 — the Prophet's ﷺ supplication on entering the toilet: refuge from 'khubuth and khaba'ith' (Anas)
Sahih Muslim 2018 — naming Allah on entering the house (Jabir)
Sunan Abi Dawud 5082 — the three quls, morning and evening (hasan per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: What We Know, and What We Do Not
chapters.body: The honest answer: the Qur'an says Shaytan and his tribe see us from where we do not see them (7:27), and the Prophet ﷺ said that every one of us has an assigned companion from the jinn (Muslim 2814). When he entered the toilet he would say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the khubuth and the khaba'ith' — male and female evil spirits (Bukhari 142, from Anas). Beyond this, the sources checked for this card do not say whether the jinn are in your room tonight or where they live, and this card does not guess. Now the question the question is really asking — am I in danger? — and the revealed answer is a set of habits, not an investigation: say Bismillah on entering your house (when a man mentions Allah on entering, Shaytan says to his companions that they have no place for the night — Muslim 2018, from Jabir), and recite the three quls morning and evening (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani) and Ayat al-Kursi at night (Bukhari 3275). You are not told to be afraid of the unseen; you are told to keep Allah in mind, and that is what the Prophet ﷺ taught.

familyQuestion: You are known and seen by Allah wherever you are. What habit of remembering Him could you add to your night?

title: Will Allah forgive my worst sin?
subtitle: The Qur'an names one thing it does not forgive if a person dies upon it
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — 'Allah forgives all sins'
Qur'an 4:48 — 'Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills'
Qur'an 25:68-70 — 'And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity ... those who repent'

chapters.heading: The Short List
chapters.body: The Qur'an is clear about the one thing that is not forgiven if a person dies upon it: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (4:48) — and repentance before death from shirk is accepted: 'Say to those who have disbelieved [that] if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them' (8:38). The even harder case the Qur'an names directly: those who never invoked another god, nor killed a soul forbidden by Allah, nor committed adultery — 'Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful' (25:68-70). Murder and zina — replaced with good deeds for the one who turns. In the hadith of Abu Sa'id, the man among the Children of Israel who had killed ninety-nine people was told by a knowledgeable man that nothing stands between him and repentance (Bukhari 3470). Apart from dying upon shirk (4:48), the Qur'an places no sin beyond Allah's forgiveness for the one who turns back to Him.

familyQuestion: The door of return is open until death. What are you holding back from bringing to it?

title: Why do bad things happen to good people?
subtitle: The question of the test — and of meanings deferred
sources: Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity'
Qur'an 67:2 — the test
Qur'an 2:216 — 'perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you'
Qur'an 2:30 — 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know'
Sahih Muslim 2999 — 'amazing is the affair of the believer' (Suhaib)

chapters.heading: The Answer That Isn't an Explanation
chapters.body: The Qur'an's answer is not a philosophy of evil; it is a promise inside a test: life is '[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed' (67:2), and 'Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity' (2:286). The Prophet ﷺ gave the shape of the answer: 'Amazing is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him, and that is for no one but the believer: if prosperity reaches him he is grateful, and that is good for him; if harm reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999). Gratitude and patience: the two doors by which every event enters as good. And under it all sits a Qur'anic teaching this card names, in its own framing, 'deferred interpretation': 'Perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah Knows, while you know not' (2:216), and the verse the angels themselves answered with at the creation of Adam: 'They said, Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You? Allah said, Indeed, I know that which you do not know' (2:30). What the Qur'an gives is trust in the One who knows, not an explanation of every event.

familyQuestion: 'I know that which you do not know.' What event in your life are you judging that only Allah fully knows?

title: Are the end times near?
subtitle: Every generation is closer than the last — the signs are a syllabus, not a date
sources: Qur'an 7:187 — 'Its knowledge is only with my Lord'
Qur'an 33:63 — 'Knowledge of it is only with Allah'
Qur'an 47:18 — 'Then do they await except that the Hour should come upon them unexpectedly?'
Sahih al-Bukhari 80 — knowledge lifted, ignorance, wine, zina (Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 7121 — time passing quickly, trials and killing, abundant wealth (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 8 — barefoot goat-herds competing in tall buildings (Umar)

chapters.heading: Closer Every Day
chapters.body: The signs of the Hour are not a date but a syllabus. The Prophet ﷺ listed signs: knowledge would be lifted, ignorance would spread, wine would be drunk widely, and illicit relations become open (Bukhari 80); time would seem to pass quickly, knowledge would diminish, trials and killing would spread, and wealth would grow so abundant that a rich man would struggle to find anyone to accept his charity (Bukhari 7121); and, in the hadith of Jibril, that barefoot, destitute goat-herds would compete in constructing magnificent buildings (Muslim 8). These were reported fourteen centuries ago; the Prophet ﷺ did not give them as a way to date the Hour. The Qur'an's instruction is precise: 'They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him' (7:187). The Qur'an says knowledge of the Hour is with Allah (7:187; 33:63). The card draws no date and no conclusion about our own time.

familyQuestion: The signs are a syllabus. Which line of that syllabus is your own household failing right now?

title: Who is the Mahdi? Will Isa really return?
subtitle: Isa's return is in the hadith of Bukhari and Muslim; the Mahdi hadith is graded sound by some and disputed by others
sources: Qur'an 4:157-158 — 'Rather, Allah raised him to Himself'
Qur'an 43:61 — Isa 'will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2222 and Sahih Muslim 155 — the son of Maryam will descend as a just ruler (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3449 and Sahih Muslim 155 — 'your imam is among you'
Sahih Muslim 2937 — the report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: the descent at the white minaret east of Damascus

Sunan Abi Dawud 4282 and 4283 — a man from the Prophet's ﷺ family will fill the earth with justice (4282: hasan sahih per al-Albani, isnad hasan per Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam; 4283: sahih per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: A Return, Not a Sequel
chapters.body: The Qur'an says Allah raised Isa to Himself (4:158) and that he 'will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour' (43:61). The Prophet ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will soon descend among you as a just ruler; he will break the cross, kill the pig and abolish the jizyah, and wealth will become so abundant that no one will accept it (Bukhari 2222; Muslim 155, from Abu Hurayrah). Bukhari 3449 and Muslim 155 add: how will you be when the son of Maryam descends and your imam is from among you? The long report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an adds that he descends at the white minaret in the east of Damascus (Muslim 2937). As for the Mahdi: Ibn Mas'ud reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that if only one day of the world remained, Allah would lengthen that day until He raised a man from my family whose name is the same as mine, who will fill the earth with justice as it has been filled with oppression (Abu Dawud 4282; see also Ali's report, 4283). Al-Albani grades 4282 hasan sahih and Zubair Ali Za'i's grade is isnad hasan, but the Mahdi hadith as a whole has been disputed by some scholars, and neither Bukhari nor Muslim narrates it. Scholars also differ on the details — such as whether the Muslim leader in Isa's time is the Mahdi — and this card does not decide. Believe the return; leave every date and every identification to Allah (33:63).

familyQuestion: Isa returns to lead by the Qur'an and the Sunnah of this ummah. What does it mean for you that the Book you hold now is the Book he will rule by?

title: Who is the Dajjal?
subtitle: Every prophet warned his nation — and the Prophet ﷺ gave the community specific counsel
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3337 — no prophet but warned his nation of the Dajjal; he is one-eyed (Ibn Umar)
Sahih Muslim 2933 — the letters k-f-r between his eyes (Anas)
Sahih Muslim 809 — the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf protect from the Dajjal (Abu al-Darda)
Sahih Muslim 2946 — no creation causes more trouble than the Dajjal, from Adam to the Hour (Hisham ibn Amir)
Sahih Muslim 2937 — the report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: the Dajjal and the descent of Isa

chapters.heading: One-Eyed
chapters.body: The hadith collections report that the Prophet ﷺ said in a public address that there was no prophet but warned his nation against him — Nuh and the prophets after him (Bukhari 3337, from Ibn Umar); and he added something no earlier prophet had told their people: the Dajjal is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed (Bukhari 3337). Another report adds that the letters k-f-r are written between his eyes (Muslim 2933, from Anas). The Prophet's counsel is detailed: whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal (Muslim 809, from Abu al-Darda). The Prophet ﷺ also described the scale of the trial: from the creation of Adam until the Last Hour there is no creation that causes more trouble than the Dajjal (Muslim 2946, from Hisham ibn Amir). And the long report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an tells of the Dajjal and then the descent of Isa (Muslim 2937). The Prophet ﷺ taught his community how to prepare.

familyQuestion: Every prophet warned of him, and the exit is ten verses. When did you last read al-Kahf's opening?

title: Who are Ya'juj and Ma'juj?
subtitle: The people behind the barrier, and the promise that it will be made level
sources: Qur'an 18:94-98 — Dhul-Qarnayn builds the barrier
Qur'an 21:96 — 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend'
Sahih Muslim 2937 — al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: Allah will send Gog and Magog in the time of Isa

chapters.heading: The Iron and Copper Wall
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells their story in Surah al-Kahf. A people complained to Dhul-Qarnayn (whose identity the sources dispute; see his own story): 'indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?' (18:94). He answered, 'That in which my Lord has established me is better [than what you offer], but assist me with strength; I will make between you and them a dam' (18:95). He said: 'Bring me sheets of iron' — until, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said: 'Blow [with bellows],' until he had made it like fire, he said, 'Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper' (18:96). Gog and Magog were unable to pass over it, nor to make any penetration in it (18:97). And he said: 'This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true' (18:98). The Qur'an also says they will be released: 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend' (21:96); and the long report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an says Allah will send them after the Dajjal is killed, in the time of Isa (Muslim 2937). The sources checked give no more, and this card does not guess where the barrier is or who they are today.

familyQuestion: The barrier held by Allah's decree until the promise comes. What in your life is held by His mercy that you take for granted?

title: Will I be alone when I die?
subtitle: The room empties — and the sources describe who comes
sources: Qur'an 6:164 — 'no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another'
Qur'an 16:32 — the angels take the righteous: 'Peace be upon you'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 — the believer's glad tidings at death (Ubadah ibn as-Samit)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1374 — the two angels, and the believer's answer (Anas)
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1071 — 'Sleep as a newlywed' (hasan per al-Albani)

chapters.heading: The Room Empties
chapters.body: The Qur'an is plain that each soul stands for itself: 'no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another' (6:164). No one can die your death or say your la ilaha illa Allah for you (a reflection). But the sources do not describe a soul abandoned. The Qur'an says the angels take the righteous saying: 'Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do' (16:32). The Prophet ﷺ said that when a believer's death approaches he receives the good news of Allah's pleasure and blessings (Bukhari 6507). After burial two angels come to him and ask him (Bukhari 1374), and in Abu Hurayrah's report, when he answers well, he is told to sleep like a bridegroom whom no one wakes but the dearest of his family (Tirmidhi 1071, hasan per al-Albani). A reflection: you will not be alone with nothing; what remains with you is what you did and the One who was always there.

familyQuestion: Each of us stands for ourselves. What would you want to have done by then for the One who knows you?

title: Will anyone intercede for me?
subtitle: Three rescues on a day with no other rescuer
sources: Qur'an 2:255 — 'who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?'
Qur'an 17:79 and 82:19
Sahih Muslim 193 — the Prophet's ﷺ intercession
Sunan Abi Dawud 2522 — the martyr's intercession for seventy of his family (sahih per al-Albani)
Sahih Muslim 183 — the believers plead for their brothers in the Fire
Sahih Muslim 2732 — dua for an absent brother
Qur'an 4:85 — 'Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a reward therefrom'

chapters.heading: The Three Doors
chapters.body: The hadith of the intercession is long (Muslim 193, from Anas): on a day when a soul will not possess for another soul power to do a thing (82:19), people go to Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, and each declines, citing an error of his own; they come to Muhammad ﷺ, who says he will ask his Lord for permission, and he falls in prostration; when he is told, raise your head, O Muhammad, he praises his Lord with words he is taught, then intercedes; a limit is set, and he brings people out of the Fire into Paradise, and this happens several times (Muslim 193). The Qur'an promises that station: 'it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station' (17:79). A second door: the Prophet ﷺ said a martyr's intercession will be accepted for seventy members of his family (Abu Dawud 2522, from Abu al-Darda; sahih per al-Albani, sahih li-ghayrihi per Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut, hasan per Zubair Ali Za'i). A third: the believers plead for brothers who were fasting and praying and performing pilgrimage with them, and are allowed to bring them out (Muslim 183). And the Qur'an opens the same word downward for you: 'Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a reward therefrom' (4:85) — intercession is not only for prophets. When you make dua for your brother in his absence, the angel commissioned over it says: Amen, and for you the same (Muslim 2732).

familyQuestion: Intercession is only by Allah's permission. What are you doing now — praying for others, teaching, forgiving — that you hope to be counted?

title: Is Hell forever?
subtitle: What the Qur'an says, what the hadith adds for believers, and where scholars differ
sources: Qur'an 2:167 — 'And they are never to emerge from the Fire'
Qur'an 4:56 — 'Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment'
Qur'an 33:65 — 'Abiding therein forever'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6560 — whoever has faith equal to a mustard seed is taken out (Abu Sa'id al-Khudri)
Sahih Muslim 183 — Allah takes out a handful who never did good (Abu Sa'id al-Khudri)

chapters.heading: The Seriousness and the Door
chapters.body: The Qur'an is serious about Hell so that the way out is unmissable. For those who reject, it says: 'And they are never to emerge from the Fire' (2:167), and speaks of 'abiding therein forever' (33:65; also 4:169).
