The hadith adds a difference for believers: the Prophet ﷺ said that when the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire the Fire, Allah will say: take out whoever has faith equal to a mustard seed in his heart; they come out burnt like coal and are thrown into the river of life, where they spring up as a seed grows on the bank of a stream (Bukhari 6560); and in the long report of Abu Sa'id, after the angels, the messengers and the believers have interceded, Allah takes out of the Fire a handful who never did any good and casts them into the river of life (Muslim 183). So for the believer who enters the Fire, it is not forever. Scholars have discussed the duration of Hell for the disbelievers — some hold that it is eternal for the disbelievers on the plain wording of the verses, and other views are recorded in the scholarly literature; this card follows the verses and leaves the discussion to scholars. The door out is repentance, and its hours are the hours of your life.

familyQuestion: The door is open as long as you are alive. What would you do before it closes?

title: What is Paradise actually like?
subtitle: No eye has seen it — which is the point
sources: Qur'an 32:16-17 — those who rise at night; 'no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3244 — 'what no eye has seen and no ear has heard' (Abu Hurayrah)
Qur'an 9:72 — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow'
Qur'an 47:15 — rivers of water, milk, wine and honey
Qur'an 56:35 — 'a [new] creation'
Qur'an 18:31 — silk, brocade and bracelets

chapters.heading: The Unseen Reward for the Unseen Deeds
chapters.body: In the hadith qudsi Abu Hurayrah reported, Allah said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined (Bukhari 3244). The Qur'an's own description — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' (9:72), rivers of water, milk, wine and purified honey (47:15), companions produced 'in a [new] creation' (56:35), green garments of fine silk and brocade, and bracelets (18:31) — is given in words of this world. That the descriptions do not capture the reality is how scholars commonly read the hadith; it is an interpretation, not a report. The Qur'an also says: 'And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do' (32:17). A reflection: this can be read as hidden reward for hidden deeds; the verse itself, in context (32:16-17), is about those who rise at night to call on their Lord.

familyQuestion: Hidden deeds, hidden reward. What are you doing tonight that no eye will ever see?

title: Why do I have to pray five times a day?
subtitle: The appointment is the relationship
sources: Qur'an 20:14 — 'indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance'
Qur'an 29:45 — 'Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing'
Sahih Muslim 162 — the five prayers at the Night Journey; fifty reduced to five with the reward of fifty
Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2621 — 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer' (hasan sahih gharib per al-Tirmidhi; sahih per Darussalam)
Sunan an-Nasa'i 463 — the same hadith (sahih per Darussalam)

chapters.heading: Five Appointments with the King
chapters.body: The five prayers were gifted at the summit of the heavens during the Night Journey — fifty first, then five with the reward of fifty (Muslim 162, from Anas; each prayer is credited as ten) — and the number is the design: a day cannot pass without the servant being called back. The Qur'an gives the mechanism: 'establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14); and the effect: 'prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater' (29:45). The Prophet ﷺ drew the contract in one line: 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved' (Tirmidhi 2621, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah; sahih per al-Albani and isnad sahih per Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam; also Nasa'i 463, sahih per al-Albani) — not because the King needs the audience, but because the servant unmade by distance is the one who stops coming. A reflection: five times a day is a standing appointment, not only a duty. Scholars differ on what the saying about abandoning the prayer means for one who neglects it through laziness rather than denial (the schools differ on whether it is disbelief or a grave sin); that is a question for a scholar.

familyQuestion: The King calls five times and waits. When you delay the prayer, what are you telling the One who keeps the appointment?
